title: Best Online Bookkeepers (2026): How to Hire One Safely
description: How to hire an online bookkeeper: what the service should include, what to prepare, what drives the price and the red flags to avoid.
intro: A bookkeeper records your income and expenses, keeps accounts reconciled and gives you reports you can trust. Good books make tax time and business decisions easier. Problems come from unclear scope, access shared unsafely, or expecting tax advice from someone not qualified to give it. This guide helps you set up bookkeeping help the right way.

faq.q: What is the difference between a bookkeeper and an accountant?
faq.a: A bookkeeper records transactions and keeps accounts up to date. An accountant or tax professional prepares tax returns, gives tax advice and may sign official filings. Many businesses use both. Rules on who may file and advise differ by country.
Usually the accounting software you already use, such as QuickBooks, Xero or a local equivalent. Keep the subscription in your name and invite the bookkeeper as a user.

faq.q: How should I share bank information?
faq.a: Connect your bank feed to your accounting software yourself, or share statements. Never give a bookkeeper your online banking password. Use read-only or accountant access wherever the software allows it.

faq.q: Can they catch up on past months?
faq.a: Yes, clean-up or catch-up bookkeeping is a common service. It is usually priced by the number of months and transactions, and it takes longer if receipts are missing.

faq.q: Will the bookkeeper file my taxes?
faq.a: Only if they are qualified to do so where you are, and it is part of the agreement. Otherwise they prepare the records and your accountant files. Confirm this before you order.
